title: Counting Objects and Counting to 100
seo_title: Grade 1 Counting to 100 Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 1: Count objects; count forwards and backwards
standard_text: Count objects reliably (up to 50 by the end of the year); count forwards and backwards in ones from any number between 0 and 100.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 1 maths worksheets: counting objects, counting forwards and backwards to 100, one more and one less. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
key_sub: One more is the next number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Touch each object once as you say the number.
  • The last number you say tells you how many.
  • One more is the next number; one less is the number before.
  • Count on and count back on a number line.

Examples

Example

What comes after 39?

39, 40

Answer: 40

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting twiceTouch each object once.
SkippingSay every number in order.
Before or afterAfter means one more.

It is Ruan’s birthday. How old is he?
items.e: Count the candles. Touch each one once: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. He is 6.

items.q: Kagiso has a candle for each year. How old is he?
items.e: Count the candles once each: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. He is 7.

items.q: Thandi is 6 today. How old will she be next birthday?
items.e: Next birthday is one more year. One more than 6 is 7.

items.q: Mbali walks up these steps. How many steps are there?
items.e: Count each step once: 1, 2, 3 … 10, 11, 12. There are 12 steps.

items.q: Ofentse swims 17 lengths. Then she swims 1 more. How many lengths?
How many cars are in the car park?
items.e: Count across the top row: 7 cars. Count on along the bottom row: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. There are 14 cars.

items.q: How many empty spaces are there?
items.e: Count only the empty spaces, not the cars. Top row: 3. Bottom row: 3. 3 and 3 is 6.

items.q: Busisiwe’s coat peg is number 19. The next peg is one more. What number is it?
items.e: One more than 19 is 20. 9 ones and 1 more make 2 tens.

items.q: Kyle has 74 stickers. He gives 1 away. How many are left?
items.e: One less than 74 is 73. 75 would be one more.

items.q: Thabo is on page 60. He turns back 1 page. What page is he on?
items.e: One less than 60 is 59. Not 69: going back 1 from 60 goes down to 5 tens.
Count each row: A has 6, B has 9, C has 7, D has 4. Row B has 9. That is the most.

items.q: Apples for break. Which row has the fewest apples?
items.e: Count each row: A has 8, B has 7, C has 10, D has 5. Row D has 5. That is the fewest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. 41 is 4 tens and 1 one. So 41 is more than 14.

items.q: Which row has more than 10 balls?
items.e: Count each row: A has 12, B has 9, C has 10, D has 8. Row A has 12. That is the only row with more than 10.
Count on from 12 to 17: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. That is 5 jumps. Lwazi has 5 more. Do not add: 17 and 12 is 29.
Count each row: A has 14, B has 11, C has 15, D has 13. Row C has 15. That is the most.
Count on from 9 to 15: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 6 jumps. Chloe has 6 fewer.

items.q: These cards show stickers. Who has the fewest stickers?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 13 has only 1 ten. Do not read 13 as 31. The smallest number is 13. Busisiwe has the fewest.

items.q: These cards show how many shells each child found at the beach. Who found the most shells?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 42 has 4 tens and 2 ones. 40 has 4 tens and 0 ones. The biggest number is 42. Lindiwe has the most.

items.q: The class has 26 learners. There are 30 chairs. How many more chairs than learners?
items.e: Count on from 26 to 30: 27, 28, 29, 30. That is 4 jumps. There are 4 more chairs. Do not add: 26 and 30 is 56.
